newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: SOCCER-AUSTRIA LOSE KUEHBAUER FOR SCOTLAND MATCH.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-AUSTRIA LOSE KUEHBAUER FOR SCOTLAND MATCH.

text.p: Austria will be without midfielder Dietmar Kuehbauer of Rapid Vienna for next Wednesday's important World Cup group four qualifier against Scotland in Glasgow.

Kuehbauer was not considered for Herbert Prohaska's 18-man squad, which was announced on Thursday, after he opted to stay in Austria with his wife Michaela who is currently in a coma following a car crash.
Prohaska is also keeping a careful watch on Werder Bremen striker Heimo Pfeifenberger who is nursing a broken toe.
Casino Graz's Dieter Ramusch is on standby to take over if Pfeifenberger cannot play against Bayern Munich in a Bundesliga match at the weekend.
Austria are currently second in the group standings, one point behind Scotland.
However they had their confidence badly shaken 10 days ago when they lost their first international since November 1995 -- a shock 2-0 defeat by Slovenia in Linz.
"The only positive thing about the match against Slovenia was that, because it was a friendly, we did not lose three points," said Prohaska.
"But it would not have scared the Scots even if we had won against Slovenia. They have always believed they can beat us in Glasgow."
Goalkeepers: Michael Konsel (Rapid Vienna), Franz Wohlfahrt (VfB Stuttgart)

Defenders: Wolfgang Feiersinger (Borussia Dortmund), Michael Hatz (AC Reggiana), Goran Kartalija (Linzer ASK), Walter Kogler (SV Salzburg), Anton Pfeffer (Austria Vienna), Peter Schoettel (Rapid Vienna)
Midfielders: Franz Aigner (SV Salzburg), Andreas Heraf (Rapid Vienna), Andreas Herzog (Werder Bremen), Markus Schopp (Hamburg), Peter Stoeger (Rapid Vienna)
Strikers: Heimo Pfeifenberger (Werder Bremen), Harald Cerny (1860 Munich), Anton Polster (Cologne), Ivica Vastic (Sturm Graz), Arnold Wetl (FC Porto)
